claim_reviews.source_based_rationale: The four inputs identify operator/period, unit and denominator, source and destination, and distinct source classes; each can be applied to another target.

The Connecticut Humanities broadside image states company, address and February date; Connecticut Humanities attributes image to UConn. Seton Guide p. 65 indexed full text identifies catalogue and prospectus; Christie lot 5084352 specifies a different November directory. The LOC and UConn frame endpoints were not retrievable; no independent copy is implied.

Direct facsimile inspection yields 11, 3, 2, 8, 20, 4, 2 rows = 50; Tyler and Flour entries and prospective office-hours change are visible. Reusable instructions require recording unit and duplicate policy.

1878 broadside lists Police Office. 23 March 1880 Journal and Courier p. 1 reports police telephone notification but not provider, caller location or route. Evening Mercury 2 September 1886 p. 2 reprints New Haven Register report of a call from SNET executive office to New York; merchant availability was prospective and no January 1878 connection is implied.

De Land 1907 §VI, NPS landmark page and Census Telephones and Telegraphs p. 66 differ on dates/units; 1968 Bell Labs Record p. 46 caption says 21 customers on eight lines. Kingsbury pp. 74–75 transcribes Ponton prospectus and reports failure to establish the plan. These are separate dated accounts, not interchangeable direct ledgers.

Bell US174465 claim 5 is a producer patent dated 1876; Coy US224653 specification is a different patent granted 1880. De Land §VI reports Bell licence and telephone use, while Seton p.65 inventories a prospectus; neither verifies shipment, contract or January switch design. Both endpoints and alternative routes are investigated; no historic link asserted.

NHFPL microfilm and Yale Register guide list stated access; De Land 1907 §VI election returns suggest targeted issue window, not an inspected original account. UConn finding aid and Yale News access limitation identify concrete follow-up, not a completed search of unavailable originals.

The rejection criteria distinguish repeated source, listings vs uptake, and unresolved network route; the stopping rule and independent Finland service anchor make the pilot reusable. Decision preserves unexplained January discrepancy and rejects linking the 1880 notification to the specific exchange.

The actual dated operator broadside identifies New Haven District Telephone Company, 219 Chapel Street, listings and stated hours; it is a contemporary text and a distinct dated documented-description event from existing January availability, not a duplicate.

Independent visual row tally confirms 50 listed rows including 11 residence rows, with ditto and repeated-name method and no inferred subscriber or household count. February event is correctly attached.

The 1880 newspaper source does not show which company or route handled notification and the February broadside alone cannot establish adoption speed. Sourced status and removed unsupported immediate reception do not silently upgrade other reviewed claims.

Source records correctly distinguish the operator broadside and separate contemporary press report; sampled image byte SHA-256 matches descriptor. The 1880 newspaper report provides independent limited reporting, not named exchange use.

No new graph relation. Bell patent source and New Haven recipient were tested at instrument-family level, but exact transmission and January switch lineage remain unproven; Coy 1880 patent cannot date installation. The selected Radiolinja target is a separate future pilot, not evidence for invention.
